name: Omega Healthcare Investors, Inc.
sector: Real Estate / Healthcare REIT (skilled nursing & senior housing)
moat_justification: Scale and diversification are real (80+ operators, ~900 skilled nursing / senior housing properties, long triple-net leases with ~2% escalators, BBB- access to unsecured debt) but the triple-net healthcare REIT model is replicable, pricing power stops at contractual escalators, and returns are a levered real-estate spread hostage to operator credit and Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement. Filing evidence: gross margin and roic_proxy are not computable from the filed tags (no COGS / operating income tagged in recent years), and ROE ran only 6.8%-12.2% over FY2021-25 — not well above the cost of capital through a cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 7.7%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.3x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.7%) vs bull-case tier C (10.9%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable but commodity healthcare REIT, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% on any scenario (weighted IRR 9.1%, IV@15% $23.78 vs $45.64 price); it only clears 15% at ~$23.78, roughly half the current price.
moat_for: Scale: ~900 properties across 80+ operators diversifies single-tenant rent risk
Long-term triple-net leases with contractual ~2% escalators; TTM operator EBITDAR coverage improved to 1.65x (Q2 2026)
Investment-grade (BBB-) unsecured capital access; leverage cut to 3.3x net debt/adjusted EBITDA, revolver nearly undrawn
Demographic tailwind: aging population drives skilled nursing / senior housing demand with low new supply
moat_against: Triple-net model is replicable — no network effects, no pricing power beyond contractual escalators
Tenant credit is the business risk: Genesis bankruptcy, CommuniCare exit ($480M sale of 18 facilities in Q2 2026), Maplewood stress
Growth is bought with constant equity issuance — diluted shares +7.7%/yr, so per-share OE was flat FY2021-25 despite revenue growth
ROE only 6.8%-12.2% FY2021-25; no ROIC history above the cost of capital in the filed data
